# Send-ZbxProxyData

## SYNOPSIS

Sends one page of history values as an active proxy.

## SYNTAX

```
Send-ZbxProxyData [-ProxyName] <string> [-Server] <DnsEndPoint[]> [-History] <ZabbixProxyHistoryItem[]> [-More] [-ProxyDelay <long>] [-Version <Version>] [-Tls <ZabbixTlsMode>] [-PskIdentity <string>] [-Psk <SecureString>] [-Certificate <string>] [-CertificateKey <string>] [-CertificateAuthority <string>] [-CertificateRevocationList <string>] [-ServerIssuer <string>] [-ServerSubject <string>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Send-ZbxProxyData cmdlet sends the history values in -History to the server's trapper once, as the active proxy named in -ProxyName, with no session running, and writes the server's answer. The server takes values only for hosts that the proxy monitors, and only after its configuration cache has loaded the proxy. Start-ZbxActiveProxy keeps a proxy session running instead. -WhatIf shows what would be sent.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Push one value as an active proxy

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
$entry = New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -ItemId $item.ItemId -Value 42
Send-ZbxProxyData -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051' -History $entry | Select-Object Response, Info, Upload
```

One 'proxy data' request on its own connection, no session. The server takes values only for items of hosts the proxy monitors. Zabbix 7.0 answers 'failed' (current proxy version is not supported): this cmdlet announces 7.4.0.

### Example 2: Push several values through the pipeline

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
$start = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddMinutes(-3).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
0..2 | ForEach-Object { New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -ItemId $item.ItemId -Value (10 * $_) -Clock ($start + 60 * $_) } |
    Send-ZbxProxyData -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051' | Out-Null
Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
Get-ZbxHistory -Id $item.ItemId -SortField clock | Select-Object Clock, Value
```

The piped entries are gathered and sent as one page in one request. -Clock stamps a value in the past (Unix seconds); Get-ZbxHistory reads the values back once the server has written them.

### Example 3: Say that more is held behind this page

```powershell
$item = Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Key -eq 'app.requests'
$page = 1..3 | ForEach-Object { New-ZbxHistoryDataEntry -ItemId $item.ItemId -Value $_ }
Send-ZbxProxyData -ProxyName 'proxy-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051' -History $page -More -ProxyDelay 120 |
    Select-Object Response, Upload
```

-More tells the server another page follows at once; -ProxyDelay is how old, in seconds, the oldest value still held is. Both are what a proxy that fell behind reports; the response's Upload says whether the server wants more.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixProxyHistoryItem[]`: Bound to -History (ByValue). One value as proxy data carries it: by item id, with its id — the store's sequence, which the server de-duplicates on — and its state.

## OUTPUTS

- `ZabbixProxyResponse`: What the server answers a proxy data or proxy config with.
